newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE SHARES SURGE TO NEW LEVELS, SEEN BULLISH.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE SHARES SURGE TO NEW LEVELS, SEEN BULLISH.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares rose almost one percent to scale new levels in active trade on Tuesday, propelled by continuing bullish sentiment underpinned by high liquidity.
The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's main industrial index surged 102.11 points -- or 0.9 percent -- to break through the key psychological 11,000 barrier and close at a new all time high of 11,095.53.

"The market is showing no real sign of slowing down. We expect it to continue strong," one broker said, adding investors were preferring to put their money in equities on the back of little movement in interest rates on the money market.
"Liquidity has been high and this money has to find a home. Institutions are underweight in equities so they are pushing up prices because they have to get stock," another broker said.
Among Tuesday's winners, merchant banker FMB -- whose shareholders approved on Monday its merger with locally-owned Heritage Investment Bank -- soared 500 cents to 5,000.

Pharmaceutical group Caps also surged 500 cents to 3,000, hotels, supermarkets and beverages conglomerate Delta rose 50 cents to 1,900 while finance house UDC at 290, tea and coffee producers EHPL at 300 and cable manufacturer BICAF all gained 25 cents.
Hotel and supermarket group Meikles added 20 cents to 3,075 and horticultural group Ariston saw a special bargain of 2.7 million shares traded at 210 cents.
A couple of counters bucked the trend, notably bankers Barclays which dropped 60 cents to 3,250 and merchant bankers NMB which shed 50 cents to 3,500.
Minings were quiet and easier as bullion continued sluggish.
Wankie Colliery lost 10 cents to 600 and the mining index ended 3.74 points to 860.21.
